subject: yc-safe-premoney
citation: The Y Combinator pre-money safe — the "original safe" — in its four published US variants, together with the SAFE Primer. Introduced by Y Combinator in late 2013 and superseded on 2018-09-28 by the post-money safe. No longer published by Y Combinator; recovered from the Internet Archive.
in_force_absent_reason: A standard form has no in-force date and no currency banner. This one has less than that: unlike the post-money forms it carries no version stamp either — every word/header*.xml and word/footer*.xml part of all four .docx is empty but for a page-number field (source/footers.json). So the documents state no currency, no edition and no date, and the only fixed point is the Wayback capture timestamp on each document below.
note:
SOURCES ONLY. There is no encodings/ row under this subject and none is planned in this change; the pre-money arithmetic is deferred to the paper track, where these are the texts van der Meyden and Maher analysed. Four things the schema has no field for.

(1) NOTHING WAS REACHED DIRECTLY. Y Combinator no longer hosts these forms, so every document is retrieval_method 'archive' with its capture URL and 14-digit timestamp. All five were re-fetched from the Internet Archive on 2026-09-04 and every sha256 matched the deposited copy, from both the plain capture URL and the byte-exact `id_` form.

(2) THE CAPTURE TIMESTAMPS ARE NOT A SINGLE VINTAGE. The four forms are 2014-10-06 captures taken within about ten minutes of each other; the Primer is 2017-09-10, nearly three years later. They are deposited together because they are one product line, not because they were published together.

(3) A WAYBACK LOOKUP QUIRK, RECORDED SO THE NEXT PERSON DOES NOT CONCLUDE 'NOT ARCHIVED'. The availability API at http://archive.org/wayback/available normalises the queried URL in a way that is case-sensitive in the first path token: `?url=ycombinator.com/docs/SAFE_cap.docx` and `?url=ycombinator.com/docs/SAFE_Primer.rtf` return the capture, while `?url=ycombinator.com/docs/SAFE_cap_discount.docx` and `?url=ycombinator.com/docs/SAFE_MFN.docx` return an EMPTY archived_snapshots — and `safe_cap_discount.docx` and `safe_MFN.docx` return them. The captures exist in every case; only the lookup differs. The archive_url on each document below was fetched and is what should be used.

(4) THERE IS NO LICENCE TO RECORD, AND THAT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. These forms carry no copyright notice and no licence line anywhere — not in the headers or footers, not in the body, and the string "Y Combinator" does not appear in any of the four. The CC BY-ND footer was added at post-money v1.0 in 2018 (User Guide, Appendix III). Terms are UNDETERMINED; SOURCE-LICENSE.md says what that does and does not permit.

The .md conversions and SAFE_Primer.txt are DERIVATIONS, not retrievals, so they are not listed as documents: the .md by `pandoc <file>.docx -t gfm --wrap=none` (pandoc 2.9.2.1, reproduces byte-for-byte), the .txt by macOS `textutil -convert txt` because pandoc cannot read RTF. Both are digested in source/SHA256SUMS. No retrieval_cost is recorded: the fetch did not measure itself and a fabricated zero would be worse than the silence.

documents.title: Pre-money SAFE — Valuation Cap, no Discount
documents.citation: Y Combinator, "Valuation Cap, no Discount" (the original safe), published at http://www.ycombinator.com/docs/SAFE_cap.docx; superseded on 2018-09-28 by the post-money safe. The form carries no version stamp and no date of its own.
documents.covers_absent_reason: The form states no range of law and carries no version stamp, so there is nothing on its face to date it. What IS pinned is the capture: this is the state of that URL at 20141006184551. Whether the text changed between the publisher's late-2013 introduction and that capture has not been checked, so no range can honestly be written.

documents.title: SAFE Primer
documents.citation: Y Combinator, "SAFE Primer", published at http://www.ycombinator.com/docs/SAFE_Primer.rtf. The pre-money era's counterpart to the post-money SAFE User Guide: why, when and how to use a safe, a Q&A, an Appendix I of alternative versions and an Appendix II of worked examples.
documents.covers_absent_reason: A primer states no range of law. Note that it is captured three years later (2017-09-10) than the four forms (2014-10-06), so the two are not necessarily the same vintage and nothing here establishes that they are.
